# Preface {.unnumbered}

Welcome to **Entropy-Based Learning**. This short book is an introductory, evolving companion to a research program on *modern entropy- and energy-based
learning*, developed at the [Blue Whale Lab](https://bluewhale.yataobian.com/)
led by [Yatao Bian](https://yataobian.com/).

Entropy is one of the deepest bridges between physics, information theory, and
machine learning — a single quantity reinvented, again and again, for heat
engines, telephone lines, quantum ensembles, and even theories of human anxiety.
Three complementary principles organize the material in this book:

- **The Maximum Entropy Principle** — among all models consistent with the
  observed constraints, prefer the one that is maximally noncommittal (highest
  entropy). This principle underlies statistical physics and Boltzmann
  machines, and it defines a family of learning methods that includes a
  principled class of game-theoretic valuations, neural set functions learned
  from their optimal subsets, and maximum-entropy and inverse reinforcement
  learning. With a pretrained model as the base measure, the same family
  contains energy-based guidance at inference time and post-training methods
  such as RLHF, GRPO, and DPO.
- **The Minimum Entropy Principle** — when a model's own predictions can serve
  as a training signal, reducing predictive uncertainty can elicit capabilities
  such as reasoning, *without* external supervision. It elicits but does not
  add capability, since the training loop never touches ground truth, and,
  left unchecked, it collapses the model onto one confident answer, right or
  wrong.
- **The Minimax Entropy Principle** — maximize entropy given the features a
  model includes, then choose the features that make that entropy as small as
  possible [@zhu1997minimax; @carcamo2025minimax]. This couples the two
  principles above, and the same nesting answers two questions: *what to
  measure*, by choosing the features that give the shortest description of
  the data, and *what to commit to*, by minimizing the entropy of a
  prediction, which is what a softmax classifier with a linear head already
  does.

Binding them together is the **free energy** $F = U - TS$, in which temperature $T$ 
sets the exchange rate between energy and entropy. It is the equation that
carried statistical physics into machine learning, 
and it makes the three
principles above three settings of one dial rather than three separate
doctrines. 

## How complete is this draft? {.unnumbered}

:::{.callout-warning title="Work in Progress"}
This book is an ongoing project, released early so you can follow its development. Most chapters are incomplete. The table below shows the current status of each chapter. Please keep this in mind before quoting or citing any part of the text, or before judging drafts that are still being written.
:::


| Chapter | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 — Introduction | early draft |
| 2 — Entropy and the Maximum Entropy Principle | **mostly complete** |
| 3 — Energy, Entropy, and Free Energy | **mostly complete** |
| 4 — Energy-Based Models | **mostly complete** |
| 5 — Maximum-Entropy Learning | **mostly complete** |
| 6 — Minimum-Entropy Learning | **mostly complete** |
| 7 — Minimax-Entropy Learning | first full draft |
| 8 — Energy-Based Guidance and Refinement | first full draft |
| 9 — Maximum-Entropy Post-Training | first full draft |
| 10 — Entropy-Based Learning for Science | early draft |
| 11 — Summary | early draft |

"Mostly complete" means the argument is in place and has been checked, though details may still move. "First full draft" means the chapter is written end to end but has not yet been checked with the same care. "Early draft" means little more than a
scaffold. The table will be updated as chapters mature. Feedback and contributions are
welcome at any stage.

A printable PDF of the current draft is available from the download button in the sidebar, or directly as [Entropy-Based-Learning.pdf](assets/Entropy-Based-Learning.pdf).

To learn more about the underlying research, visit
<https://yataobian.com/> and the Blue Whale Lab.
